title: Maharashtra in Maps
author: K. R. Dikshit; assisted by Charulata Patil
publisher: Maharashtra State Board for Literature and Culture, Bombay
supports: Chapter XIII identifies the North-to-Deccan approach via the Burhanpur gap and Tapi crossing, with Dhule–Malegaon or Jalgaon–Aurangabad routes; it identifies Aurangabad–Solapur–Bijapur, Aurangabad–Ahmadnagar–Pune, and Bijapur–Karad–Chiplun–Guhagar as strategically important traditional routes. It states that these routes assumed added importance in the late seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
caveat: Retrospective regional synthesis, not a 1622 itinerary or surveyed historical road map. Its use of 'Aurangabad' is later than the scenario's Khirki-era naming. The statement about routes gaining importance cautions against assuming identical traffic or maintenance in 1622.

title: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, Poona District, Volume III, Communications and Traffic
publisher: Bombay Presidency; reprint by Maharashtra State Gazetteers
supports: Pages 109–110 describe the Poona–Nasik road, branches to Junnar, the Malsej route via Belha/Ale/Otur/Madh, Junnar–Ghatghar–Nana pass, and pack-animal trade with the Konkan.
caveat: Nineteenth-century description. It establishes later route use and names, not continuous operation, exact alignments or facilities in 1622.

title: The Imperial Gazetteer of India, 2nd edition, Volume II, entry 'Bhor Ghat'
supports: Describes Bhor Ghat as a key Deccan gateway, pack-bullock traffic before carriage-road construction, artillery access improvements in 1804 and the 1830 carriage-road opening.
caveat: Retrospective source; it does not date the old pack track to 1622 or provide its precise seventeenth-century alignment.

title: Lohagad and Visapur
supports: States that Lohagad and Visapur guarded the trade route through Bor Ghat between the Arabian Sea and the Deccan; dates Visapur's construction to 1713–1720.
caveat: General tourism description; does not provide a dated 1622 command record. Visapur is later than the scenario and is not inserted into this corridor.

title: Nane Ghat (नाणेघाट)
publisher: Marathi Vishwakosh / Maharashtra Rajya Marathi Vishwakosh Nirmiti Mandal
supports: Ancient Nane Ghat's Desh–Konkan trade role, Junnar-side connection and historic pass setting.
caveat: Modern reference article, not a 1622 itinerary or daily traffic record.

title: Poona District Gazetteer, Places of Interest: Jivadhan Fort
supports: Jivdhan described as commanding Nane Ghat; records Nizam Shahi fort status until the dynasty's extinction and inclusion in a Mughal transfer in 1637.
caveat: Does not identify a 1622 killedar, daily traffic or exact seventeenth-century control of the approach.

title: Malshej Ghat
publisher: District Administration, Thane, Government of Maharashtra
supports: Present Malshej location on the Kalyan–Nagar road and current route from Junnar via Narayangaon.
caveat: Present road alignment; not proof of a 1622 route or equivalence with every older Malsej spelling/alignment.

title: Malshej Ghat
publisher: Department of Tourism, Government of Maharashtra
supports: Describes Malshej as a mountain pass and references historic strategic movements and old trade routes.
caveat: General historical statement; no 1622 route date, exact alignment or operational details.

title: Region Pack 01 Batch 02A — forts.json and related files
supports: Exact IDs fort_daulatabad, fort_lohagad, fort_jivdhan and referenced site IDs site_khirki, site_ahmadnagar, site_pune, site_solapur, site_junnar.
caveat: Project data provides IDs and associations, not independent proof of historical route alignments.

title: Region Pack 01 Item 01 — new sites additions
publisher: User-supplied project data / prior generated pack
supports: Exact ID site_malavli and its association with fort_lohagad.
caveat: Site addition is a map anchor only; it does not prove the exact road centreline or a seventeenth-century settlement classification.
